$comment: Contract between Tiled exports and the game. Both the runtime map registry (src/assets/maps.ts) and the build-time validator (scripts/validate-maps.mjs) read this file, so a Tiled export that drifts from it fails the build instead of rendering an empty floor.
$layerOrderComment: The render model (ADR-125). Every map has exactly these seven layers, in this order (empty allowed): ground (roads, floors) · ground_detail (markings, grates, baked shadows) · buildings (wall tiles) · sorted (the Y-sort band: an OBJECT layer of everything that stands on the ground — typed placed objects, `cutout` images with a baseY + footprint, `above` images drawn over the street) · props_above (overhead tiles: wires, awnings, canopies, roofs) · collision (invisible: a tile stencil, or an object layer of pixel rects for generated maps) · fx. Plus `spawns`, an object layer of points and zones outside the draw order.
$sortedComment: sorted objects: `type` = an ObjectDef id (placed object, tiles or sprite; depth from its footprint bottom), `cutout` (properties image, baseY, footprint x/y/w/h — a static body; depth = baseY), or `above` (property image; drawn at the props_above depth, never collides). Written by scripts/import-map.mjs and generate-street-map.mjs.
$collisionComment: collision as an object layer (generated maps): rects with property kind = building | prop. Buildings cover the whole wall footprint except door gaps.
$pulseLayerComment: Optional per-map `pulseLayer`: an object layer of City Pulse slots. Every slot is a named, uniquely named object with a `type` (wall, corner, shopfront, crowd). Districts list the slots they offer under pulse_slots and the validator checks they exist.
$doorComment: Any spawn-layer object named door_* or typed `door` is a door and must be 32x48 (player height = door height, design system §2). The map validator warns otherwise.
$sopComment: `sop: true` marks a map migrated to the render model: every cutout needs a footprint and legacy occluders are errors. Unmigrated maps get warnings until their A5 re-audit.
